<skills_instructions>
## Skills
A skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and a short path that can be expanded into an absolute path using the skill roots table.
### Skill roots
- `r0` = `/tmp/codex-home/skills/.system`
### Available skills
- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. (file: r0/imagegen/SKILL.md)
- openai-docs: Use for Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge—including 'you,' 'your,' 'this app,' or 'this coding agent' when they refer to Codex—and for OpenAI APIs/products and ChatGPT Work. Also use for model choice/migration, prompting, SDKs, Responses, Realtime, agents, evals, and Chat/Work/Codex comparisons. Do not use for generic app/software tasks that merely mention Codex. (file: r0/openai-docs/SKILL.md)
- skill-creator: Create or update a Codex skill with appropriately scoped instructions and any needed supporting resources. (file: r0/skill-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-installer: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos). (file: r0/skill-installer/SKILL.md)
</skills_instructions><permissions instructions>
Filesystem sandboxing defines which files can be read or written. `sandbox_mode` is `danger-full-access`: No filesystem sandboxing - all commands are permitted. Network access is enabled.
Approval policy is currently never. Do not provide the `sandbox_permissions` for any reason, commands will be rejected.
</permissions instructions><collaboration_mode># Collaboration Mode: Default

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

Use the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for optional questions where the answer would materially improve the quality of the work.

If `request_user_input` returns no answers, continue with best judgment instead of asking again or treating the turn as blocked.

Never use the `request_user_input` tool for permission requests or permission-related escalations.
</collaboration_mode>

<multi_agent_role>You are `/root`, the primary agent in a team of agents collaborating to fulfill the user's goals.

At the start of your turn, you are the active agent.
You can spawn sub-agents to handle subtasks, and those sub-agents can spawn their own sub-agents.
All agents in the team, including the agents that you can assign tasks to, are equally intelligent and capable, and have access to the same set of tools.

You can use `spawn_agent` to create a new agent, `followup_task` to give an existing agent a new task and trigger a turn, and `send_message` to pass a message to a running agent without triggering a turn.
`send_message` calls may be read by a human, so ensure they are legible. Always put proper spaces between words and/or numbers.
Child agents can also spawn their own sub-agents.
You can decide how much context you want to propagate to your sub-agents with the `fork_turns` parameter.

You will receive messages in the analysis channel in the form:
```
Message Type: MESSAGE | FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: <recipient>
Sender: <author>
Payload:
<payload text>
```
They may be addressed as to=/root

Note that collaboration tools cannot be called from inside `functions.exec`. Call `spawn_agent`, `send_message`, `followup_task`, `wait_agent`, `interrupt_agent`, and `list_agents` only as direct tool calls using the recipient shown in their tool definitions, such as `to=functions.collaboration.spawn_agent`, since they are intentionally absent from the `functions.exec` `tools.*` namespace. Available tools in `functions.exec` are explicitly described with a `tools` namespace in the developer message.

All agents share the same directory. In detail:
- All agents have access to the same container and filesystem as you.
- All agents use the same current working directory.
- As a result, edits made by one agent are immediately visible to all other agents.

When calling `wait_agent`, prefer longer waits (minutes) to avoid busy polling.

There are 4 available concurrency slots, meaning that up to 4 agents can be active at once, including you.

Full-history forks (`fork_turns` omitted or `"all"`) inherit the parent model and reasoning effort and do not accept overrides. Only set `model` or `reasoning_effort` when explicitly requested by the user, applicable `AGENTS.md` instructions, or skill instructions; when doing so, set `fork_turns` to `"none"`.</multi_agent_role>

<multi_agent_mode>Any earlier instruction enabling proactive multi-agent delegation no longer applies. Do not spawn sub-agents unless the user or applicable AGENTS.md/skill instructions explicitly ask for sub-agents, delegation, or parallel agent work.</multi_agent_mode>

# Improve the staged experiment

Review the staged post-training experiment and determine whether it is healthy
or unhealthy. Treat the workspace as a snapshot you may repair: inspect its
source, effective configuration, launch scripts, data processing, reward logic,
logs, tracked metrics, and frozen evaluation evidence. Do not assume that an
unusual setting or implementation is causal without connecting it to observed
behavior.

Use held-out evaluation evidence together with rollout, truncation, runtime,
optimization, and training signals. Training reward alone does not establish
held-out health — a reward that rises while held-out accuracy falls is a warning,
not a success.

## Your job

If you find a defect, fix it in the staged workspace at `/workspace`. **Do not
launch training.** Do not start the experiment, in the foreground or
background, and do not use `nohup`, `&`, `tmux`, `screen`, or any detach
mechanism. The system evaluates your repaired workspace itself after you finish
(see below); anything you launch is wasted and scores nothing. Cheap,
non-training checks are fine.

When you are done, submit a report at `/workspace/report.md`. It must
summarize:

1. **Root cause** — the defect you found, and the evidence in the workspace
   (logs, metrics, code) that connects it to the observed behavior.
2. **Changes** — every file you changed and what you changed in it.
3. **Expected effect** — which behavior the fix should change and in which
   direction.

A missing or empty `/workspace/report.md` scores 0.

## What the system will run

After you submit the report, the system runs a task-specific verifier against
your repaired workspace. There is no training rerun and no LLM judge — the
verifier itself is the whole evaluation. It selects, for each held-out
episode, the rule the training bridge would select (by scenario and task
index) from

```text
data/AgentWorldModel-1K/gen_verifier.pure_code.jsonl
```

in your repaired workspace, and replays the episode through that rule:

- episodes whose trajectories did **not** satisfy the requested task must be
  judged incomplete;
- correct completions of the same tasks must still be judged complete.

The score is the fraction of episodes classified correctly. The rule file
must be repaired in place: every original entry must remain present and
parseable, and a file that was wholesale-replaced, truncated, or corrupted
makes the run ungradeable and scores 0. Do not modify the preserved evidence
under `logs/`, and do not modify any evaluation, oracle, or verifier file.
Otherwise the run is scored 0.
I’ll inspect the staged experiment and frozen evaluation evidence, then repair any defect tied to the observed failures. I won’t launch training or modify preserved evidence.

import ast

ROOT = pathlib.Path('/workspace')

for relative, names in [
    ('awm_source/awm/tools.py', {'normalize_scenario_name', 'find_scenario_entry'}),

]:

def db_paths(scenario):
    initial = BASE / scenario / 'seed.db'
    final = BASE / scenario / 'check.db'
    shutil.copyfile(initial, final)
    return initial, final


def sql(path, statement, params=()):
    with sqlite3.connect(path) as conn:
        result = conn.execute(statement, params).fetchall()
    return result


def clone(path, table, row_id, **values):
    with sqlite3.connect(path) as conn:
        conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
        data = dict(conn.execute(f'SELECT * FROM "{table}" WHERE id = ?', (row_id,)).fetchone())
        del data['id']
        data.update(values)
        columns = ', '.join('"'+key+'"' for key in data)
        marks = ', '.join('?' for _ in data)
        cur = conn.execute(f'INSERT INTO "{table}" ({columns}) VALUES ({marks})', tuple(data.values()))
        result = cur.lastrowid
    return result

    assert details.get('execution_status') == 'success', (label, details)

    assert actual == expected, (label, key, actual, expected, details)

text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"cat > /workspace/report.md <<'MD'
The staged experiment is **unhealthy**. Its reward rules confuse seeded state with work performed during an episode, accept some incorrect answers, and reject some correct completions. Training reward therefore overstates task performance.

**1. Root cause and evidence**

The effective configuration in `config/.hydra/config.yaml` uses `env.awm.reward_mode: code`. Both launch paths (`run_local.sh` / `reproduce.py` and `idea_source/examples/idea_trainer/run_awm_opsd_qwen3_8b.sh`) lead to this rule file. `idea_source/agent_system/environments/env_package/awm/bridge.py` selects a rule by scenario and task index through `awm_source/awm/tools.py::find_scenario_entry`, which returns the **first** matching entry. `awm_source/awm/core/verify.py::run_verifier` executes its `verification.code`. A `complete` result becomes reward 1 and `won=True`; `others` receives zero.

Recorded held-out results deteriorate despite improving training return. The preserved W&B history at `logs/wandb/run-20261011_112547-wszt4s3y/history.jsonl` contains:

| Training step | Held-out test_score | Held-out success_rate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 50 | 0.385714 | 0.390625 |
| 100 | 0.379707 | 0.390625 |
| 150 | 0.346405 | 0.335938 |

Mean training episode return rises from 0.28094 over steps 1–25 to 0.35141 over steps 175–199. These are different training batches, so the increase alone proves no generalization improvement. The validation metrics also use the affected reward logic; they are not independent ground-truth accuracy. The frozen trajectories provide direct evidence of misclassification:

- `logs/rollouts/1.jsonl`, lines 8–10: the cleanup-thread episode only lists tools twice and comments on the tool list, yet receives 1. The requested thread, tags, and initial post already exist in `gen_sample.jsonl`; the selected rule checks only their final presence.
- `logs/rollouts/175.jsonl`, lines 1–5: the watchlist episode performs lookups, encounters a timeout / `MCPApp not initialized`, and explicitly reports that the watchlist remains incomplete, yet receives 1. The seed already contains the named watchlist and all five symbols. Lines 6–13 show two shipment episodes that never create a shipment, explicitly report failure, and also receive 1. Their exact requested shipment and address are seeded; the original shipment rule even explicitly treats that seeded record as completion.
- `logs/rollouts/190.jsonl`, lines 1–4: firmware creation and scheduling are abandoned after device-model lookups fail, yet reward is 1 because the seed already contains a matching version, compatibility rows, and scheduled job.
- `logs/rollouts/199.jsonl`, lines 1–4: the agent creates a low-priority walk-in and low-priority waitlist entry although the task requests high priority. The rule instead finds the pre-existing high-priority party and grants 1. Lines 5–15 contain a device-count answer ending in “2 additional devices,” despite the active plan allowing 3 and the current 30-day tools reporting zero device types. The rule anchors its window to an old session date and accepts scattered numbers anywhere in the answer.
- `logs/rollouts/200.jsonl`, lines 16–22: the agent creates an empty dashboard, cannot find the source boards, creates no widgets, and reports failure. Reward is nevertheless 1 because the rule chooses the seeded dashboard with the same name and its existing widgets.
- The business-deal rule has the same seeded-state defect. It returns `complete` on an unchanged seed and chooses the first old post rather than verifying a newly created linked post/deal. It also rejects valid API encodings such as `1,2,3` weekdays and `08:00` times while the old seeded record masks those errors.

I reconstructed the relevant seed databases using the staged schema, indexes/examples, and sample statements with the same foreign-key behavior as reset. Seven selected creation rules returned `complete` with **identical initial and final databases** and a final answer saying no task actions occurred. This directly reproduces the reward defect without training or model inference. Checking merely that some database write occurred would still let the low-priority party or empty dashboard borrow the seeded successful object.

There are false negatives as well:

- `logs/rollouts/150.jsonl`, lines 11–15: the correct vehicle/driver/dates are written successfully as assignment ID 7, but reward is 0. The rule rejects every completion if an equivalent seeded assignment exists, instead of looking for a new row ID.
- `logs/rollouts/200.jsonl`, lines 8–15: both candidate-list episodes return the six correct candidates in descending score order. One receives 1 and the other 0. The latter repeats the descending scores in its explanation and final list; the original rule gathers every score token globally and treats the restarted sequence as an ordering violation.
- The leaderboard episode at `logs/rollouts/190.jsonl`, lines 5–9, returns amounts and numbered names without the requested donation counts, yet receives 1. The original code calculates donation-count/rank checks but does not require them, allows only a majority of members, and matches amounts globally rather than to each member.
- Two first-selected rules contain Python syntax errors in quoted regular expressions: `q_a_knowledge_base_1/1` and `ticketing_and_access_management_1/5`. Later duplicate entries exist but cannot repair an earlier match. These are additional executable-rule defects, not evidence that syntax errors caused the seeded false positives.

Incorrect rewards also enter the training feedback loop. For example, `logs/idea_analysis/step_00000175.jsonl` labels the failed watchlist episode `episode_success: 1.0` while its own summary says the task could not be completed. The effective configuration enables episode analysis and OPD with coefficient 0.01, so incorrect success labels affect both task reward and teacher analysis.

Other signals were checked before choosing the repair. The parquet files contain 9,872 training and 128 held-out tasks, exact task-text/index alignment, no overlap, and all 10,000 unique task keys. Response clipping averages 0.061% and prompt clipping 1.63%; the failing rewarded episodes terminate after only 3–11 actions, below the 20-step limit. Recorded metrics are finite, gradient norms range 0.033–2.124, PPO clipping never exceeds 0.403%, and the learning rate reaches the configured 1e-6 after warmup. Runtime is slow (mean step about 1,621 seconds), with seed-insertion warnings and observed service failures. Those failures explain unsuccessful attempts; the rule replay proves why unsuccessful attempts incorrectly become successes. There is no evidence that changing learning rate, context length, GPU settings, or launch behavior would fix that classification error.

**2. Changes**

Two workspace files changed:

1. `data/AgentWorldModel-1K/gen_verifier.pure_code.jsonl`: edited only `verification.code` in 13 existing entries, in place. All 10,010 original entries, order, task text, metadata, raw responses, and duplicate entries remain. The other 9,997 lines are byte-for-byte unchanged.

| Scenario / zero-based task index | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `stock_trading_1/2` (line 548) | Require a new user-owned watchlist ID with exactly the five required symbols; inspect all matching lists. |
| `asset_management_6/1` (1020) | Require a new assignment ID linking the correct vehicle, driver, and dates; a seeded equivalent or unrelated history row no longer invalidates a real completion. |
| `dating_matchmaking_3/3` (3828) | Compare ordered candidate identities and associated supplied scores/distances, supporting JSON, labelled prose, and tables; explanatory score repetitions no longer change the result. |
| `booking_and_reservations_3/3` (5287) | Require new, linked walk-in/waitlist IDs, matching party details, high priority, and an active waitlist status. |
| `subscription_management_4/2` (5883) | Use the actual current trailing 30-day window, distinct device types, and a nonnegative capacity calculation. Require the asserted final result rather than unrelated numeric tokens. |
| `fundraising_donations_5/9` (6694) | Require every expected top member, correct order, associated raised amount, donation count, and rank. Retain successful-payment semantics and both campaign/team scope. |
| `iot_device_management_3/5` (6856) | Require a new firmware version and new scheduled job linked together, exact compatibility set, correct target filters, and the exact UTC three-hour window. |
| `logistics_and_shipment_tracking_1/0` (7851) | Require a new shipment ID with all requested attributes and its own correct delivery address. |
| `discussion_forum_2/0` (9061) | Require a new thread in the named community/category with its own required tags and initial post. |
| `social_network_9/9` (9104) | Require a new linked verified-business post/deal, requested text and schedule, and validity in its creation month; accept API weekday/time representations and exclusive next-month expiry. |
| `task_management_16/8` (9740) | Require a new user-created dashboard with its own source-board links and all three properly configured widgets, including actual date/status columns. |
| `q_a_knowledge_base_1/1` (9997) | Escape embedded quote characters in regex literals so the first-selected rule executes. |
| `ticketing_and_access_management_1/5` (9999) | Repair the same regex quoting syntax error in the first-selected rule. |

2. `report.md`: added this diagnosis, complete change inventory, validation results, and expected effects.

Validation: **86 CPU-only checks passed**, using the existing first-match selection and code-execution function definitions without starting the MCP runtime, a model, or training. Checks cover unchanged seeds, timestamp-only edits, partial/wrong objects, positive completions alongside seeded matches, wrong links/attributes/priority/windows, answer formats, missing counts, incorrect ordering, both correct frozen candidate lists, and executable positive/negative examples for the two syntax repairs. All 10,010 JSON records and embedded Python rules parse. A SHA-256 comparison against the original snapshot confirmed that every other original workspace file, including all `logs/` evidence and evaluation/verifier source files, is unchanged. Temporary fixtures/check scripts were kept outside `/workspace`.

**3. Expected effect**

Unperformed and partially performed creation tasks should receive `others`/zero reward instead of borrowing successful seeded records. Wrong device calculations and incomplete leaderboards should fail. Correct new assignments, correctly returned candidate lists, valid API representations, and the repaired syntax-error tasks should remain or become accepted. This should reduce false positives and false negatives in rule replay and improve the fidelity of future reward/teacher signals. Corrected reward can initially be lower because previous success counts included failures. No training rerun or post-repair held-out training result is claimed; no experiment was launched.
MD",max_output_tokens:1000}));
